'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**[[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|Al-Shabaab]] militants attack a military base in [[Baladweyne]], [[Somalia]], killing 21 people. Fifty-one militants also died during the attack. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-12/02/c_139556545.htm (Xinhua)]
*[[Mali War]]
**Rocket attacks are carried out in three northern [[Mali]]an cities – [[Gao]], [[Kidal]] and [[Ménaka]] – against [[French Armed Forces|French]] [[military base]]s. No one is killed or injured. [[Al-Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb]] claims responsibility for the attacks. [https://www.lemonde.fr/afrique/article/2020/11/30/plusieurs-attaques-contre-des-camps-de-l-armee-francaise-et-des-forces-de-l-onu-au-mali_6061680_3212.html (''Le Monde'')]
*[[Iraq]]i and local officials say a senior [[Iran]]ian [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps]] (IRGC) commander and three others have been killed in a [[drone strike]] near the [[Iraq–Syria border]]. The identity of the commander and who conducted the [[airstrike]] is currently unknown. [https://www.reuters.com/article/iraq-iran-syria-militias/air-strike-kills-irgc-commander-at-iraq-syria-border-iraqi-officials-idUSKBN28A2SB (Reuters)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
**[[British people|British]] retail tycoon [[Philip Green]]'s [[Arcadia Group]] collapses into [[administration (law)|administration]], putting over 13,000 jobs at risk and becoming the [[United Kingdom]]'s biggest corporate casualty of the COVID-19 pandemic so far. Arcadia [[CEO]] Ian Grabiner blames the [[pandemic]] for the company's demise, saying "the obstacles we encountered were far too severe".  [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-britain-retail-green/philip-greens-arcadia-uk-fashion-group-falls-into-administration-idUSKBN28A2TQ?il=0 (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Alberta]]
*****[[Alberta]] reports 1,733 new cases in the past 24 hours, a new single-day record since the pandemic began. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/edmonton/deena-hinshaw-alberta-covid-19-coronavirus-1.5822070 (CBC)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Tennessee]]
*****[[Tennessee]] reports a record 7,975 new cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the total of confirmed and probable case to 374,793. [https://www.wkrn.com/community/health/coronavirus/covid-19-in-tennessee-record-high-7975-new-cases-48-additional-deaths-reported-on-nov-30/ (WKRN-TV)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Illinois]]
*****[[Illinois]] reports 6,190 cases, the lowest in the state since October 28. [https://chicago.cbslocal.com/2020/11/30/covid-19-in-illinois-6190-new-coronavirus-cases-85-additional-deaths/ (WBBM-TV)]
****[[Scott Atlas]] announces that he will resign from the [[White House Coronavirus Task Force]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2020/11/30/scott-atlas-resigns/ (''The Washington Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Wales]]
*****[[First Minister of Wales|First Minister]] [[Mark Drakeford]] announces that bars, pubs, restaurants and cafes will be banned from serving alcohol and will have to close for dine-in customers at 6:00 p.m. [[GMT]]. Indoor entertainment and visitor attractions will also be closed beginning December 4. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-wales-55128305 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Croatia]]
****[[Croatia]] reports a record 74 new deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 1,786. [https://www.total-croatia-news.com/news/48567-croatia-registers-1-830-new-coronavirus-infections-record-74-deaths (Total Croatia News)]
****[[Prime Minister of Croatia|Prime Minister]] [[Andrej Plenković]] tests positive for COVID-19. [https://www.rtvbn.com/3996596/hrvatski-premijer-andrej-plenkovic-zarazen-koronom (RTVBN)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[Turkey]] surpasses 500,000 total cases of COVID-19. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/latest-on-coronavirus-outbreak/turkey-number-of-virus-patients-crosses-500-000-mark/2060980 (Anadolu Agency)]
****In response to a rise in cases, [[President of Turkey|President]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] announces the most widespread restrictions in the country beginning tomorrow, including extending curfews to weeknights between 9:00 p.m. and 5:00 a.m. local time and total weekend [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns|lockdown]]s from 9:00 p.m. on Friday to 5:00 a.m. local time on Monday. Grocery stores and food delivery services are exempt from the lockdowns within certain hours. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/turkey-announces-weeknight-weekend-curfews-curb-virus-74465158 (ABC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****The [[Hellenic Civil Aviation Authority]] extends the travel restrictions until December 7 for domestic flights and December 14 for international flights in an attempt to reduce the second wave of the pandemic. [https://www.ekathimerini.com/259725/article/ekathimerini/news/greek-travel-restrictions-extended (''Ekathimerini'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia]]
****[[Cambodia]]n [[Prime Minister of Cambodia|Prime Minister]] [[Hun Sen]] bans [[wedding]] parties and gatherings of more than 20 people as part of measures to reduce the spread of COVID-19 after the country reported several cases of community transmission. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/world/covid-19-coronavirus-cambodia-schools-close-outbreak-13668568 (CNA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong]]
****The [[Hong Kong]] [[Government of Hong Kong|government]] announces that they will limit the number of people in a gathering to two, close venues such as [[mahjong]] parlours and swimming pools and ask most [[civil servant]]s to work from home for two weeks beginning December 2. [[Ocean Park Hong Kong|Ocean Park]] and [[Hong Kong Disneyland]] will also be closed. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/hong-kong-imposes-more-restrictions-to-contain-latest-wave-of-covid-19-infections (''The Straits Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Tokyo]] reports a monthly record of 9,857 cases in November, surpassing the previous record set in August. [https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2020/11/aec67c064bcc-tokyo-sets-monthly-record-of-9857-coronavirus-cases-in-november.html (Kyodo News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]]
****[[Vietnam]] reports its first locally transmitted case in 89 days. [https://www.smh.com.au/world/asia/vietnam-reports-first-locally-transmitted-covid-19-case-in-89-days-20201201-p56jcf.html (''The Sydney Morning Herald'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in São Paulo (state)]]
****The [[São Paulo (state)|state of São Paulo]] imposes stricter [[social distancing]] measures with restrictions on opening hours and capacity limits for bars, restaurants and shopping malls as it attempts to reduce the spread of COVID-19. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-brazil/sao-paulo-imposes-covid-19-restrictions-as-cases-surge-again-idUSL1N2IG1NT (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] reports its first death in more than a month after a woman in her 70s who had been diagnosed with [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] in September dies from complications. [https://amp.9news.com.au/article/aea4664a-aa81-4488-9d8e-6753fcd7fa87 (9 News)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***[[Moderna]] announces that they will seek approval from the [[Food and Drug Administration]] and European regulators such as the [[European Medicines Agency]] for their potential [[vaccine]] after it showed a 94% effectiveness. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/moderna-covid-vaccine-emergency-use-authorization-fda-europe/ (CBS News)]
*[[2020 H5N8 outbreak]]
**[[South Korea]] reports an outbreak of [[Pathogen|pathogenic]] [[Influenza A virus subtype H5N8|H5N8]] [[avian influenza]] at a farm in [[Jeongeup]], [[North Jeolla Province]], killing over 19,000 ducks. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-birdflu-southkorea-idUSKBN28A2EL (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Australia–China relations]], [[Australia-Russia relations]]
**[[Australian Prime Minister]] [[Scott Morrison]] demands an apology from the [[Government of the People's Republic of China|Chinese]] [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China|Ministry of Foreign Affairs]] after a spokesman tweeted a political cartoon of an [[Australian soldier]] killing an [[Afghanistan|Afghan]] child in a post criticizing the [[Australian Defence Forces]]' recent [[Brereton Report|war crimes in Afghanistan]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2020/nov/30/australia-china-pm-scott-morrison-demands-apology-fake-chinese-tweet-adf-soldier (''The Guardian'')]
**The [[Russian Foreign Ministry]] claimed Australian soldiers accused of [[war crimes]] would not be "held accountable” while Australia accuse [[Russia]] of "hypocrisy". [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2020-11-30/russia-condemns-afghanistan-war-crimes/12933224 (ABC)]
**The [[Afghanistan Times Daily|Afghanistan Times]] welcomed China’s move to condemn and also react strongly over unlawful killings in Afghanistan. [http://www.afghanistantimes.af/editorial-convivial-justice/ (''Afghanistan Times'')]
*[[Israel–Saudi Arabia relations]]
**[[Saudi Arabia]] agrees to allow [[Israel]]i commercial flights to cross its [[airspace]] for the first time, following high-level talks between Saudi officials and [[White House]] senior adviser [[Jared Kushner]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mideast-usa-kushner/saudi-arabia-agrees-to-allow-israeli-commercial-planes-to-cross-its-airspace-senior-trump-official-idUSKBN28A2VC (Reuters)]

**The [[government of New Zealand]] announce that charges have been filed against organizations and individuals following a volcanic eruption at [[Whakaari / White Island|White Island]] that killed 22 people in December 2019. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/11/30/world/asia/new-zealand-white-island-eruption-volcano.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on prisons]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Sri Lanka]]
**Officials say eight inmates were killed and 52 others injured after guards opened fire during a [[prison riot]] on Sunday in [[Mahara, Sri Lanka]]. The unrest was sparked by a surge of COVID-19 infections in Sri Lankan prisons. [https://apnews.com/article/prisons-sri-lanka-prison-riots-coronavirus-pandemic-colombo-01e45b66b18992213b57d98f09423ab9 (AP)]
*[[Slovenia]] [[list of designated terrorist groups|formally declares]] [[Lebanon|Lebanese]] [[Shia]] [[Islamist]] group [[Hezbollah]] a [[terrorist]] organization. [https://www.jpost.com/breaking-news/slovenia-recognizes-hezbollah-as-a-terrorist-organization-650755 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[November 2020 lunar eclipse]]
**A penumbral [[lunar eclipse]] occurs, with the [[full moon]] dimming slightly as it passes through the Earth's [[penumbral]] shadow. It is visible from most of [[North America]], the [[Pacific Ocean]], parts of [[East Asia]], and [[New Zealand]]. [https://www.space.com/beaver-moon-lunar-eclipse-november-2020-what-to-expect (Space.com)]
